title: When the Contact Turns Revisited
premise: Lior Lockridge, a disgraced intelligence analyst fired from three agencies, receives a calendar invite to a dead-drop meeting scheduled by Handler Vess Karrow—dead for two years. Following it, Lior uncovers the Continuum, the off-books training network that manufactured analysts like them and now erases its graduates one by one. Hunted by former classmates turned cleaners, Lior assembles a found family of other 'retired' assets to expose and burn the Continuum's archive before dawn extraction flight 9-Bravo carries the evidence—and their last chance at belonging—out of reach. In the end, Lior chooses to stay grounded, destroying the flight manifest and inheriting Vess's role not as handler but as protector of the survivors.
about_author: Mirabel Underhill is a former records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing declassified files in a basement archive before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who were trained to disappear and decided not to.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Lior Lockridge, three firings deep into obscurity, receives a calendar invite from Vess Karrow—confirmed dead since 2019—for a meeting tomorrow at a shuttered transit depot. POV: Lior. The beat is dread laced with longing: the first time in five years anyone has wanted to see them.

chapters.title: Depot Nine
chapters.summary: At the depot, Lior finds no Vess—only a burner phone preloaded with a single contact and a photograph of Lior's own personnel file, redacted except for the word CONTINUUM. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: vertigo, realizing their invisibility was engineered, not earned.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Lior reconstructs their training through flashbacks: the safehouse school where children learned tradecraft under a woman called Mother Meridian. Present-day Lior decodes the burner's first message: 'You were never bounced. You were seeded.' POV: Lior with interstitial memory. Beat: grief reframing humiliation as design.

chapters.title: The Other Graduates
chapters.summary: Following the phone's breadcrumb, Lior meets Sefa Okonkwo, a former Continuum courier running a laundromat front, who confirms four graduates have died this year—all ruled accidents. POV: Sefa. Beat: wary kinship between two people trained never to trust.

chapters.title: Cleaner at the Door
chapters.summary: A Continuum cleaner named Brant arrives at Sefa's flat; the two escape through service tunnels after Lior's counter-surveillance training kicks in. POV: alternating Lior/Sefa. Beat: terror sharpening into competence—the old training finally serving Lior instead of owning them.

chapters.title: Vess's Dead Drop
chapters.summary: A posthumous letter from Vess, hidden in a library microfiche cabinet, reveals she faked her death to build a case against Mother Meridian and named Lior her successor because Lior was the graduate who kept asking why. POV: Vess (letter) framed by Lior. Beat: inheritance—being chosen by the dead.

chapters.title: Mother Meridian
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Lior watches Meridian rewrite a rulebook overnight and punish the child who noticed. Present-day Meridian, alive and powerful, briefs her board that the 'Lockridge asset' has activated. POV: split young Lior / Meridian. Beat: cold dread meeting the architect of their brokenness.

chapters.title: The Laundromat Cell
chapters.summary: Lior, Sefa, and two more survivors—paranoid ex-signals officer Dev and medic Anouk—form an improvised cell in the laundromat basement, mapping Continuum safehouses. POV: ensemble via Lior's observation. Beat: fragile warmth; the first taste of found family, immediately distrusted.

chapters.title: Flight 9-Bravo
chapters.summary: Dev intercepts chatter about extraction flight 9-Bravo leaving at dawn in nine days, carrying the Continuum's full archive offshore beyond subpoena. POV: Dev. Beat: ticking clock installed; hope and doom fused into one departure time.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Roster
chapters.summary: Lior uses their seeded credentials to book themselves onto 9-Bravo's passenger manifest as a returning asset, discovering their own name was already listed—Meridian expects them. POV: Lior. Beat: the trap and the door are the same shape.

chapters.title: Anouk's Ledger
chapters.summary: Anouk reveals she treated Continuum casualties for years and kept a secret ledger naming every operative, including Brant's real identity and Meridian's legal alias. POV: Anouk. Beat: guilt transmuted into purpose; the cell gains its weapon.

chapters.title: Brant's Offer
chapters.summary: Brant corners Lior alone and offers reinstatement, revealing Meridian ordered Vess's death and promising Lior the belonging they always craved. POV: Lior. Beat: temptation—the seductive pull of the family that made them, set against the family they're building.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Lior confesses to the cell that they reported Sefa's mentor for defection during training, causing his death. The group fractures. POV: Lior. Beat: rock bottom—chosen family tested by inherited sin.

chapters.title: Sefa's Verdict
chapters.summary: Sefa confronts Lior at the depot, then chooses to stay: 'We were all weapons. I'm judging what you do now.' The cell re-forms with new rules written openly, revisable by vote. POV: Sefa. Beat: forgiveness as structural choice, echoing the theme of rewritten rules done right.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Recon confirms the Continuum archive is physically aboard 9-Bravo in a hardened cargo pod, guarded by six cleaners including Brant. Anouk drafts the burn plan. POV: Anouk. Beat: resolve hardening into operational clarity.

chapters.title: Meridian's Parley
chapters.summary: Meridian summons Lior to a neutral-site tea, offering succession and confessing Vess begged for Lior's life once. Lior refuses, and Meridian orders the flight moved up twelve hours. POV: dual Lior/Meridian. Beat: the mother-figure unmasked; stakes compressed.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours
chapters.summary: The cell scrambles: Dev jams hangar comms, Sefa forges ground-crew credentials, Anouk stages a medical emergency to clear the tarmac. POV: rotating. Beat: breathless competence-porn momentum, family functioning as one organism.

chapters.title: Boarding
chapters.summary: Lior boards 9-Bravo among returning assets, walking past Brant, and reaches the cargo pod as the engines spool. POV: Lior. Beat: isolation inside the machine that raised them—alone even in a crowd of mirrors.

chapters.title: Burn Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Climax: Lior torches the archive pod mid-taxi while Brant, choosing Vess's memory over Meridian, holds the cabin door. The plane aborts; cleaners scatter; Meridian's board scatters evidence that now points back at her. POV: Lior/Brant. Beat: fire as both destruction and liberation.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Dawn on the tarmac: Lior declines the extraction seat offered by a sympathetic federal contact, choosing to stay and testify rather than vanish. POV: Lior. Beat: the inversion of a lifetime's training—visibility as courage.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Months later, Lior testifies as Meridian's network unravels publicly; graduates worldwide receive letters inviting them to a support collective instead of a debrief room. POV: Lior. Beat: inheritance fulfilled—rules rewritten in daylight, by consent.

chapters.title: When the Contact Turns Revisited
chapters.summary: Epilogue: at the rebuilt depot, now the collective's home, Lior answers a knock and opens the door to a frightened new arrival holding a familiar-looking invitation. POV: Lior. Beat: cyclical closure—the contact turns again, but this time someone kind is on the other side.
